ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p485/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p485/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p485/r7.claim: Morning and evening may stand for remembrance throughout all time by naming its two ends; Ibn ʿAbbās instead specifies dawn and night prayers, al-Akhfash the period between afternoon and evening, and Qatāda dawn and afternoon prayers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p485/r7.anchor: والوقتان كناية عن جميع الزمان، ذكر الطرفين إشعار بالاستغراق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p485/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p485/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p485/r8.claim: Remembrance may encompass every act of obedience; the author then singles out prayer as glorification, especially dawn and night prayers because they are harder to perform.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p485/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الأمر بالذكر وإكثاره تكثير الطاعات والإقبال على الطاعات

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r2.claim: Against hypocrites' and mischief-makers' opposition, believers should disregard the uproar and increase remembrance and praise of God by night and day.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r2.anchor: while disregarding their rumpus they should engage more and more in remembering God and in extolling Him by night and by day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r3.claim: God's remembrance is believers' shield against Satan; Qur'anic calls to persevere against enemies repeatedly direct believers to prayer, whose link to perseverance is discussed elsewhere in the tafsīr.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r3.anchor: the real shield through which believers have to counter the onslaught of Satan and his progeny is God’s remembrance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r4.claim: In ‘glorify Him morning and evening,’ prayer is the specific after the general: remembrance is constant, while God and His Messenger set prayer times within this morning-evening timetable.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r4.anchor: Here حیتسب symbolizes the prayer. It is in fact the mention of the specific after the general.

BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r1.claim: The Persian verses portray spiritual attraction: divine light remains when lamps fade, and the inwardly perceptive see the eternal sun in an atom and the whole sea in a drop.
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r1.anchor: شمها ون شد كذاره نوراوست مغزها مى بيند اودر عين وست بيند اندر ذره خورشيد بقا بيند اندر قطره كل بحررا

BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r2.claim: Bursevi asks God for spiritual acts that bring blessings, since God fulfills needs.
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r2.anchor: نسأل الله الحركات التي تورث البركات إنه قاضي الحاجات

QASHANI:33:41-43/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:33:41-43/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:33:41-43/r2.claim: Glorifying God entails transcending acts, attributes, and Essence.

QASHANI:33:41-43/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:33:41-43/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:33:41-43/r3.claim: Morning begins with the heart's light and the lower self's darkness receding; the spirit's sun sets in annihilation of Essence, so remembrance continues from then to everlasting annihilation.
QASHANI:33:41-43/r3.anchor: وقت طلوع فجر نور القلب وإدبار ظلمة النفس وليل غروب شمس الروح بالفناء في الذات

QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r5.claim: Morning and evening glorification is described in two terms so that remembrance does not become tiresome.
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r5.anchor: التسبيح من قبيل الذكر ، ولكنه ذكره بلفظين لئلا تعتريك سآمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r1.claim: Tasbīḥ here means praying to God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r2.claim: Morning refers to the dawn prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r2.anchor: {بكرة} يعني: صلاة الصبح، {وأصيلا} يعني: صلاة العصر.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r3.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi includes noon, afternoon, and the two evening prayers under aṣīlan.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي: "وأصيلا" صلاة الظهر والعصر والعشاءين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r4.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r4.claim: Mujahid says the command means reciting the listed formulas of remembrance; tasbīḥ stands for its companion formulas.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يعني: قولوا سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر، ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله، فعبر بالتسبيح عن أخواته.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r5.claim: Another view says these formulas are the abundant remembrance, recited by the ritually pure, the sexually impure, and those in minor impurity.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r5.anchor: وقيل: المراد من قوله: "ذكرا كثيرا" هذه الكلمات يقولها الطاهر والجنب والمحدث

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r1.claim: Morning and evening are singled out for remembrance because they are especially excellent and witnessed, just as tasbīḥ is singled out among remembrances because it is their core.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r1.anchor: وتخصيصهما بالذكر للدلالة على فضلهما على سائر الأوقات لكونهما مشهودين كأفراد التسبيح من جملة الأذكار

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r2.claim: One view directs both verbs to morning and evening.

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r3.claim: Another view interprets tasbīḥ here as prayer.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r3.claim: Glorifying God means declaring Him above any contradiction of what He revealed and every defect, after affirming His perfection.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r3.anchor: أي عن أن يكون شيء على خلاف ما أخبر به , وعن كل صفة نقص بعد ما أثبتم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r4.claim: Morning and evening mean the day's beginning and end, and thus stand for remembrance at all times, since they include busy and resting periods.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r4.anchor: أي في أول النهار وآخره أي دائما لأن هذين الوقتين إما للشغل الشاغل ابتداء أو انتهاء أو للراحة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says remembrance has no prescribed limit and no excuse for omission except being overcome in one's reason.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : لم يفرض الله على عباده فريضة إلا جعل لها حدا معلوما

BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r6.claim: Dawn and dusk are witnessed by angels and signify the Hour: dusk points to the world's end and dawn to resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r6.anchor: وهما أيضا مشهودان بالملائكة ودالان على الساعة : الثاني قربها بزوال الدنيا كلها , والأول على البعث بعد الموت

BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r7.claim: An alternative interpretation is the dawn and afternoon prayers; keeping them despite competing rest and work shows great love of worship and leads to other acts by a fortiori reasoning.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r7.anchor: وبجوز أن يكون ذلك إشارة إلى صلاتي الصبح والعصر , لأن المواظبة عليهما

DURR-FULL:v6p619/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r4.speaker: مقاتل
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r4.claim: Maqatil interprets glorifying God morning and evening as praying to Him at dawn and dusk.
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r4.anchor: عن مقاتل في قوله {اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا} قال: باللسان بالتسبيح والتكبير والتهليل والتحميد واذكروه على كل حال {وسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r1.claim: Al-bukra is the beginning of the day, and al-aṣīl is the late afternoon after ʿaṣr; both words are adverbial with the two commands.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r1.anchor: والبكرة : أول النهار . والأصيل : العشي الوقت الذي بعد العصر . وانتصبا على الظرفية التي يتنازعها الفعلان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r2.claim: Mentioning morning and evening means filling the day’s portions with remembrance and glorification as far as possible; naming the endpoints signifies the whole.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r2.anchor: والمقصود من البكرة والأصيل إعمار أجزاء النهار بالذكر والتسبيح بقدر المكنة لأن ذكر طرفي الشيء يكون كناية عن استيعابه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r3.claim: Ṭarafa’s verse illustrates the rhetorical use of the two ends of something to signify its entirety.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r3.anchor: كقول طرفة : لكالطول المرخى وثنياه باليد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r4.claim: The morning is named before the afternoon because it necessarily comes first; al-aṣīl is not specially foregrounded.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r4.anchor: وقدم البكرة على الأصيل لأن البكرة أسبق من الأصيل لا محالة . وليس الأصيل جديدا بالتقديم في الذكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r5.claim: In 30:17, “you enter evening” precedes “you enter morning” because evening includes early night, which begins the Arabs’ and Islam’s reckoning of a month’s days.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r5.anchor: كما قدم لفظ { تمسون } في قوله في سورة الروم { فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون } ( الروم : 17 )

MAJAZ:v2p138/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p138/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p138/r1.claim: Bakratan wa-aṣīlan means the interval from late afternoon until night.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r1.claim: Believers should glorify God in the morning and evening, as in the verse naming the times people enter evening and morning and other parts of the day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r1.anchor: أي: عند الصباح والمساء، كقوله: {فسبحان الله حين تمسون

JISHUMI:v8p5744/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r7.claim: Bukratan wa aṣīlan are accusative adverbs of time.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r2.claim: Morning and evening means at all times.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r2.anchor: { بكرة وأصيلا } أي في كافة الأوقات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r6.claim: The commands to remember and glorify both apply to morning and evening, like saying 'fast and pray on Friday'; glorification is singled out from remembrance to mark its special merit.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r6.anchor: والفعلان ، أعني اذكروا وسبحوا موجهان إلى البكرة والأصيل ، كقولك : صم وصل يوم الجمعة ، والتسبيح من جملة الذكر ، وإنما اختصه من بين أنواعه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r8.claim: Dhikr may mean increasing good works and worship, since every obedience and good deed is remembrance; morning-evening glorification may mean all prayers, which excel other acts.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد بالذكر وإكثاره : تكثير الطاعات ، والإقبال على العبادات ؛ فإن كل طاعة وكل خير من جملة الذكر ، ثم خص من ذلك التسبيح بكرة وأصيلا وهي الصلاة في جميع أوقاتها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r9.claim: Alternatively, the morning-evening glorification means dawn and the two evening prayers because they are harder to perform and observe.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r9.anchor: أو صلاة الفجر والعشاءين ؛ لأن أداءها أشق ومراعاتها أشد .

NAHHAS:v3p316/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p316/r10.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v3p316/r10.claim: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd says aṣīl means al-ʿashī, with plural aṣāʾil; aṣl also means aṣīl, with plural āṣāl.
NAHHAS:v3p316/r10.anchor: قال محمد بن يزيد الأصيل العشي وجمعه أصائل والأصل بمعنى الأصيل وجمعه آصال

NAHHAS:v3p316/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p316/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p316/r11.claim: Another grammarian says aṣl is the plural of aṣīl, like ragīf and rughuf.
NAHHAS:v3p316/r11.anchor: وقال غيره أصل جمع أصيل كرغيف ورغف

MUQATIL:33:41-45/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:41-45/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:33:41-45/r2.claim: Morning and evening glorification means praying the dawn prayer and the noon and afternoon prayers.
MUQATIL:33:41-45/r2.anchor: يعنى صلوا بالغداة الفجر والعشى، يعنى الظهر والعصر.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r1.claim: Believers should keep their tongues busy most of the time with glorification, declaring God's oneness, praise, and magnification.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r1.anchor: أي اشغلوا ألسنتكم في معظم أحوالكم بالتسبيح والتهليل والتحميد والتكبير.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r2.claim: Mujahid says ritually pure people, those in minor impurity, and those in major impurity may say these phrases.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد: وهذه كلمات يقولهن الطاهر والمحدث والجنب.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that the command means to call upon God.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r4.speaker: جرير
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r4.claim: Jarir's verse uses sabbaha for praising God, recalling Yusuf who called upon his Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r4.anchor: قال جرير: فلا تنس تسبيح الضحى إن يوسفا دعا ربه فاختاره حين سبحا

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r5.claim: Another view says the command means to pray morning and evening, since prayer is also called tasbih.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r5.anchor: وقيل: المراد صلوا لله بكرة وأصيلا والصلاة تسمى تسبيحا.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r6.claim: Dawn, sunset, and night prayer are singled out because they especially merit encouragement and fall at the edges of the night.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r6.anchor: وخص الفجر والمغرب والعشاء بالذكر لأنها أحق بالتحريض عليها، لاتصالها بأطراف الليل.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r7.speaker: قتادة والطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r7.claim: Qatada and al-Tabari say the reference is to the dawn and afternoon prayers.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة والطبري: الإشارة إلى صلاة الغداة وصلاة العصر.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r8.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r8.claim: Al-Asil means evening, its plural is asāʾil, and al-asl is a synonym with plural āsāl.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r8.anchor: والأصيل: العشي وجمعه أصائل. والأصل بمعنى الأصيل، وجمعه آصال قاله المبرد.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r9.claim: Another grammarian says asl is the plural of asil, like ragif and ragif's plural.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r9.anchor: وقال غيره: أصل جمع أصيل كرغيف ورغف.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r10.claim: Because this verse is Medinan, it does not support the claim that prayer was first prescribed as two daily prayers at the day's ends; that report is weak and should be disregarded.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r10.anchor: هذه الآية مدنية، فلا تعلق بها لمن زعم أن الصلاة إنما فرضت أولا صلاتين في طرفي النهار. والرواية بذلك ضعيفة فلا التفات إليها

RAZI-FULL:v25p186/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p186/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p186/r1.claim: Remembering God should take the form of glorifying Him and declaring Him free of every evil; this is the intended sense of tasbih.
RAZI-FULL:v25p186/r1.anchor: فينبغي أن يكون ذكركم إياه على وجه التعظيم والتنزيه عن كل سوء وهو المراد بالتسبيح

RAZI-FULL:v25p186/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p186/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p186/r2.claim: An alternative interpretation takes tasbih here to mean prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v25p186/r2.anchor: وقيل المراد منه الصلاة وقيل للصلاة تسبيحه بكرة وأصيلا

RAZI-FULL:v25p186/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p186/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p186/r3.claim: Mentioning morning and evening as the two endpoints implies continuous remembrance, since mentioning the endpoints can convey the whole interval.
RAZI-FULL:v25p186/r3.anchor: مريد العموم قد يذكر الطرفين ويفهم منهما الوسط

RAZI-FULL:v25p186/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p186/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p186/r4.claim: He illustrates this rhetorical implication with the Prophet's mention of the first and last without the middle, which conveys comprehensive scope.
RAZI-FULL:v25p186/r4.anchor: كقوله عليه السلام ( لو أن أولكم وآخركم ) ولم يذكر وسطكم

TAB-FULL:v19p124/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says remembrance has no fixed limit or ordinary excuse for omission, unlike other duties; believers remember and glorify God in every condition, and God and the angels then pray for them.
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا} [الأحزاب: 41] يقول: " لا يفرض على عباده فريضة إلا جعل لها حدا معلوما

TAB-FULL:v19p124/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r3.claim: Qatāda identifies the morning and evening glorifications with the dawn and afternoon prayers.
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا} [الأحزاب: 42] صلاة الغداة، وصلاة العصر

TABATABAI:33:41-44/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r3.claim: Tasbīḥ means declaring God transcendent; like remembrance it need not be verbal, though saying phrases such as سبحان الله is one form of it.
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r3.anchor: التسبيح هو التنزيه وهو مثل الذكر لا يتوقف على اللفظ وإن كان التلفظ بمثل سبحان الله بعض مصاديق التسبيح.

TABATABAI:33:41-44/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r4.claim: Morning means the day's beginning and evening its later part after ʿAṣr; these periods suit glorifying God beyond changing conditions and passing defects, and together may signify continual praise, as in 41:38.
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r4.anchor: وتقييد التسبيح بالبكرة والأصيل لما فيهما من تحول الأحوال فيناسب تسبيحه وتنزيهه من التغير والتحول وكل نقص طار

TABRISI:33:42-43/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:42-43/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:42-43/r1.claim: The command to glorify God morning and evening covers early morning and evening time.
TABRISI:33:42-43/r1.anchor: أي ونزهوه سبحانه عن جميع ما لا يليق به بالغداة والعشي والأصيل العشي.

TABRISI:33:42-43/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:42-43/r2.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:33:42-43/r2.claim: Qatāda identifies the two times with the dawn and afternoon prayers.
TABRISI:33:42-43/r2.anchor: يعني به صلاة الصبح وصلاة العصر عن قتادة

TABRISI:33:42-43/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:42-43/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:33:42-43/r3.claim: Another interpretation identifies them with dawn and the final night prayer, singled out because night and day angels meet then.
TABRISI:33:42-43/r3.anchor: وصلاة الصبح وصلاة العشاء الآخرة خصهما بالذكر لأن لهما مزية على غيرهما من حيث إن ملائكة الليل والنهار يجتمعون فيهما.

TABRISI:33:42-43/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:42-43/r4.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:33:42-43/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī says morning means dawn prayer, while evening includes noon, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers.
TABRISI:33:42-43/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: أما بكرة فصلاة الفجر وأما أصيلا فصلاة الظهر والعصر والمغرب والعشاء الآخرة

THALABI:v8p51/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p51/r2.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v8p51/r2.claim: Qatādah interprets glorifying God morning and evening as the dawn and afternoon prayers.
THALABI:v8p51/r2.anchor: وسبحوه وصلوا له بكرة يعني صلاة الصبح وأصيلا يعني صلاة العصر عن قتادة

THALABI:v8p51/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p51/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v8p51/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the prayers as the afternoon prayer and the two evening prayers.
THALABI:v8p51/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يعني صلاة العصر والعشاءين

THALABI:v8p51/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p51/r4.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v8p51/r4.claim: Mujāhid says tasbīḥ here includes the phrases of praise, oneness, greatness, and reliance; these words may be said by the ritually pure, the sexually impure, and the person in minor impurity.
THALABI:v8p51/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يعني قولوا: سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:39-43/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:39-43/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:39-43/r4.claim: Glorifying God means praying to Him at dawn, afternoon, and the two evening prayers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:39-43/r4.anchor: وسبحوه } صلوا له { بكرة } صلاة الفجر { وأصيلا } صلاة العصر والعشاءين

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r1.claim: The morning and evening remembrances refer to the obligatory prayers, with morning as dawn prayer and evening as noon and afternoon prayers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r1.anchor: وأصيلا} [الأحزاب: 42] صلاة الظهر وصلاة العصر. ابن لهيعة، عن عبد الله بن هبيرة أن ابن عباس قال: هذا في الصلاة المكتوبة.

ASAD-NOTES:33:41#n52/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:33:41#n52/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:33:41#n52/r1.claim: The phrase literally means morning and evening but signifies all times.
ASAD-NOTES:33:41#n52/r1.anchor: Lit., "at morn and evening", i.e., at all times.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p119/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p119/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p119/r1.claim: Qatada identifies morning and evening glorification with the dawn and afternoon prayers.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p119/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ وسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا ﴾ قال صلاة الصبح وصلاة العصر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r1.claim: Tasbīḥ means declaring God transcendent above whatever does not befit Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r1.anchor: ونزهوه سبحانه عما لا يليق به

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r2.claim: The two terms designate the beginning and end of the day.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r3.claim: Mentioning these times does not restrict tasbīḥ to them; they are especially virtuous because night and day angels attend and meet then, and tasbīḥ is the chief form of remembrance.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r3.anchor: وتخصيصهما بالذكر ليس لقصر التسبيح عليهما دون سائر الأوقات بل لإنافة فضلهما على سائر الأوقات

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r4.claim: Another analysis directs both commands to the two day periods, like telling someone to fast and pray on Friday.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : كلا الأمرين متوجه إليهما كقولك : صم وصل يوم الجمعة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r5.claim: If much remembrance means remembering through most times, there is no need to attach the two time adverbs to the first command.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r5.anchor: وبتفسير الذكر الكثير بما يعم أغلب الأوقات لا تبقى حاجة إلى تعلقهما بالأول

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes tasbīḥ as prayer by synecdoche: morning tasbīḥ is the dawn prayer and evening tasbīḥ the night prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r6.anchor: وعن إبن عباس أن المراد بالتسبيح الصلاة أي بإطلاق الجزء على الكل والتسبيح بكرة صلاة الفجر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r7.claim: Qatāda similarly reads the times as the dawn and afternoon prayers; Alusi considers this more plausible than Ibn ʿAbbās's dawn-and-night interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r7.anchor: وعن قتادة نحو ما روى عن إبن عباس إلا أنه قال : أشار بهذين الوقتين إلى صلاة الغداة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r8.claim: One can preserve the literal sense of tasbīḥ while understanding it as performed through prayer at those times.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r8.anchor: وقد يقال : إن التسبيح على حقيقته لكن التسبيح بكرة بالصلاة فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r9.claim: It is also possible to understand remembrance as all obedience and tasbīḥ as prayer at all times, or dawn-and-afternoon or dawn-and-night prayer; Alusi considers this extension remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42#2/r9.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المراد بالذكر المأمور به تكثير الطاعات والإقبال عليها فإن كل طاعة من جملة الذكر

DURR-FULL:v6p620/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r7.claim: Qatada interprets morning and evening glorification as the dawn and afternoon prayers.
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r7.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {وسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا} قال: صلاة الصبح وصلاة العصر

DURR-FULL:v6p620/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra reports God’s instruction to remember Him for an hour after dawn and after afternoon prayer, promising to suffice the worshipper between those times.
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما يذكر عن ربه تبارك وتعالى اذكرني بعد الفجر وبعد العصر ساعة أكفك ما بينهما

DURR-FULL:v6p620/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r9.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r9.claim: Abu Umama reports that sitting in remembrance until sunrise is better than freeing two or more descendants of Ishmael, and doing so after afternoon prayer until sunset is better than freeing four.
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r9.anchor: عن أبي أمامة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأن أقعد أذكر الله وأكبره وأحمده وأسبحه وأهلله حتى تطلع الشمس

DURR-FULL:v6p620/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r10.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r10.claim: Abu al-Darda reports the Prophet urging one hundred morning repetitions of ‘Glory and praise belong to God,’ counted as a thousand good deeds; the day’s sins will not equal them and other good deeds remain abundant.
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r10.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لا يدع رجل منكم أن يعمل لله ألف حسنة حين يصبح يقول: سبحان الله وبحمده مائة مرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r4.claim: Believers should replace arguing with or insulting hypocrites over rumors about the Prophet’s marriage to Zaynab with remembrance and praise, avoiding civic strife; this is more beneficial.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r4.anchor: أن يشغلوا ألسنتهم بذكر الله وتسبيحه ، أي أن يمسكوا عن مماراة المنافقين أو عن سبهم فيما يرجفون به في قضية تزوج زينب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r5.claim: The command resembles replacing tribal boasting with remembrance after pilgrimage, and avoiding speech that could provoke retaliation against God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r5.anchor: فإذا قضيتم مناسككم فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r6.claim: The instruction also follows the command to the Prophet to leave the hypocrites’ harm aside.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r6.anchor: فهذا من نحو قوله لنبيئه { ودع أذاهم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r7.claim: If believers continue that dispute after this command, their conduct marks them as hypocrites, since believers obey their Lord.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r7.anchor: وفيه تسجيل على المنافقين بأن خوضهم في ذلك بعد هذه الآية علامة على النفاق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r8.claim: The passage opens a new address but remains connected to what precedes through contextual relevance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r8.anchor: والجملة استئناف ابتدائي متصل بما قبله للمناسبة التي أشرنا إليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r10.claim: One possible reading of tasbīḥ is supererogatory prayer, in which case it is not a specific subcategory coordinated under general remembrance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r10.anchor: يجوز أن يراد به الصلوات النوافل فليس عطف { وسبحوه } على { اذكروا الله } من عطف الخاص على العام .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r11.claim: Alternatively, tasbīḥ means saying Subḥān Allāh; it is a specially emphasized form of remembrance because it comprehensively praises God and rejects imperfections.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المأمور به من التسبيح قول : سبحان الله ، فيكون عطف { وسبحوه } على { اذكروا الله } من عطف الخاص على العام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r12.claim: On the verbal reading, tasbīḥ alludes to repudiating the hypocrites’ claims about the Prophet, like saying ‘How could we say this? Glory be to You’ at the slander.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r12.anchor: ولأن في التسبيح إيماء إلى التبرؤ مما يقوله المنافقون في حق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r13.claim: The Prophet said ‘Glory be to God; the believer does not become impure,’ illustrating the phrase as a response to an unsuitable attribution.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r13.anchor: كقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( سبحان الله المؤمن لا ينجس ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r14.speaker: هند بنت عتبة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r14.claim: When pledged not to fornicate, Hind bint ʿUtba replied ‘Glory be to God, would a free woman fornicate?’, another repudiating use of the formula.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r14.anchor: وقول هند بنت عتبة حين أخذ على النساء البيعة ( أن لا يزنين ) : سبحان الله أتزني الحرة .

BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r1.claim: A Persian couplet urges familiarity with love’s sea and purity like a shell.

BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r2.claim: Tasbīḥ means declaring God free of what does not befit Him.
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r2.anchor: ونزهوه تعالى عما لا يليق به

BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r3.claim: Al-Mufradāt defines sabḥ as swift motion through water or air; tasbīḥ is declaring God transcendent, originally rapid movement in worship, then generalized to worship by speech, action, or intention.
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r3.anchor: السبح المر السريع في الماء أو في الهواء والتسبيح تنزيه الله

BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r4.claim: Bukrah and aṣīl mean the beginning and end of the day; mentioning both endpoints implies remembrance throughout the day, especially at these honored times.
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r4.anchor: أي : أول النهار وآخره وقد يذكر الطرفان ويفهم منهما الوسط

BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r5.claim: A hadith says angels take turns among people by night and by day, witnessing the two special periods.
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r5.anchor: يتعاقبون فيكم ملائكة بالليل وملائكة بالنهار

BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r6.claim: Tasbīḥ is singled out from other forms of remembrance because it is their central element, as a form of adornment.
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r6.anchor: وإفراد التسبيح من بين الأذكار لكونه العمدة فيها من حيث أنه من باب التحلية

BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r7.claim: A hadith lists four phrases a person in major impurity should not omit: declaring God’s transcendence, praise, oneness, and greatness; the author infers that the ritually minor impure are even more entitled to say them.
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r7.anchor: أربع لا يمسك عنهن جنب سبحان الله والحمدولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر

BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r8.claim: Tasbīḥ is allowed in every state, though remembrance with ablution and purity is proper etiquette.
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r8.anchor: فلا منع من التسبيح على جميع الأحوال إلا أن الذكر على الوضوء والطهارة من آداب الرجال

BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r9.claim: Kashf al-asrār interprets morning and evening as the dawn and afternoon prayers, urging people not to let worldly work make them miss these prayers.
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r9.anchor: وسبحوه أي : صلوا به بكرة يعني صلاة الصبح وأصيلا يعني صلاة العصر

BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r10.claim: A hadith urges anyone able to avoid being overtaken by distractions from the prayers before sunrise and sunset to do so.
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r10.anchor: من استطاع منكم أن لا يغلب على صلاة قبل طلوع الشمس ولا غروبها فليفعل

BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r11.claim: Kashf al-asrār links dawn prayer to the angels’ witnessing in 17:78, and identifies the afternoon prayer as the middle prayer.
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r11.anchor: لقوله تعالى : {إن قرءان الفجر كان مشهودا} (الإسراء : 78) يعني تشهده ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r12.claim: A report says the earth cries out most intensely over unlawful blood, a bath after fornication, or someone sleeping on it before sunrise.
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r12.anchor: ما عجت الأرض إلى ربها من شيء كعجيجها من دم حرام أو غسل من زنى

BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r13.claim: God distributes provision, sends blessings, and answers prayers between dawn and sunrise, so people should not be heedless during this honored hour.
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r13.anchor: والله تعالى يقسم الأرزاق وينزل البركات ويستجيب الدعوات فيما بين طلوع الفجر وطلوع الشمس

BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r14.claim: A hadith promises the reward of a complete pilgrimage and minor pilgrimage three times over to one who prays dawn in congregation, remembers God until sunrise, and then prays two rakʿahs.
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r14.anchor: من صلى الفجر في جماعة ثم قعد يذكر الله تعالى حتى تطلع الشمس ثم صلى ركعتين

BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r15.claim: Sufi practitioners gather for remembrance after dawn prayer until the sunrise prayer; remembrance then has a powerful effect on the soul and is preferred to recitation.
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r15.anchor: ومن هنا لم يزل الصوفية المتأدبون يجتمعون على الذكر بعد صلاة الصبح إلى وقت صلاة الإشراق

BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r16.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r16.claim: Al-Qunya says blessings on the Prophet, supplication, and tasbīḥ are better than Qurʾan recitation during times when prayer is prohibited.
BURSEVI:v7p148#2/r16.anchor: من أن الصلاة على النبي عليه السلام والدعاء والتسبيح أفضل من قراءة القرآن في الأوقات التي نهى عن الصلاة فيها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda defines al-aṣīl as the period from the afternoon prayer until night.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة الأصيل ما بين العصر إلى الليل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r2.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r2.claim: On the view that the glorification means prayer, exegetes agree that the morning prayer is Fajr.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r2.anchor: أحدهما أنه الصلاة واتفق أرباب هذا القول على أن المراد بالتسبيح بكرة صلاة الفجر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r3.speaker: أبو العالية وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r3.claim: Within the prayer interpretation, Abū al-ʿĀliya and Qatāda identify the evening prayer as ʿAṣr.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r3.anchor: واختلفوا في صلاة الأصيل على ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أنها صلاة العصر قاله أبو العالية وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r4.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r4.claim: Ibn al-Sāʾib takes the evening prayers to include Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr, Maghrib, and ʿIshāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r4.anchor: والثاني أنها الظهر والعصر والمغرب والعشاء قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r5.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r5.claim: Muqātil identifies the evening prayers as Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r5.anchor: والثالث أنها الظهر والعصر قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r6.claim: The other view takes the command as spoken remembrance: saying subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh, Allāhu akbar, and lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-llāh.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p397/r6.anchor: والقول الثاني أنه التسبيح باللسان وهو قول سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله قاله مجاهد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r6.claim: If believers do this remembrance, God and His angels send blessings upon them, as the following verse says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r6.anchor: فإذا فعلتم ذلك صلى عليكم هو وملائكته

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r9.claim: The command means to declare God transcendent in the morning and evening.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r9.anchor: وسبحوه أي: نزهوه بكرة وأصيلا صباحا ومساء

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r10.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r10.claim: Qatada interprets morning and evening as the dawn and afternoon prayers.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r10.anchor: قيل: صلوا بكرة وعشيا، يعني: الصبح والعصر، عن قتادة

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r11.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r11.claim: Abu Muslim takes glorification here as declaring God above what does not befit Him.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r11.anchor: وقيل: نزهوه عما لا يليق به، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r12.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r12.claim: Abu Ali reads abundant remembrance as prayer at its morning and evening times, since prayer uniquely has appointed times and includes required remembrance; it is called glorification for its tasbīḥ.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r12.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالذكر الكثير: الذكر في الصلاة بكرة وعشيا، عن أبي علي قال: لأن الصلاة هي المختص بالأوقات والذكر

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r13.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r13.claim: The judge prefers the apparent sense, glorification as transcendence, since that is the wording’s plain meaning and is required at all times.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r13.anchor: قال القاضي: والأولى أنه أراد به التسبيح الذي هو التنزيه: لأنه ظاهر الكلام، ويجب في جميع الأحوال

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r6.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r6.claim: Qatada takes morning and evening as the dawn and afternoon prayers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r7.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash defines aṣīl as the period from afternoon until night.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r7.anchor: قال الأخفش : والأصيل ما بين العصر والليل

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r8.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r8.claim: Al-Kalbi includes the noon, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers in aṣīl.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r8.anchor: وقال الكلبي : الأصيل صلاة الظهر والعصر والمغرب والعشاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r9.claim: One sense of tasbīḥ is the specific act of declaring God transcendent.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r9.anchor: أحدها : أنه التسبيح الخاص الذي هو التنزيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r10.claim: Another sense of tasbīḥ is prayer.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r11.speaker: جرير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r11.claim: Jarir says tasbīḥ can mean supplication; a poetic line about Yunus calling on God and being rescued illustrates the sense of prayer or supplication.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r11.anchor: الثالث : أنه الدعاء , قاله جرير . فلا تنس تسبيح الضحى إن يونسا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r1.claim: Bukra is the beginning of the day and asil its end.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ وسبحوه بكرة ﴾ أول النهار ﴿ وأصيلا ﴾ آخر النهار

NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r2.claim: These times are specified because the angels of night and day meet then.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r2.anchor: وخصا بالذكر لأن ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار يجتمعون فيهما

NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r3.claim: Qatada says to recite glorification, praise, the testimony of faith, takbir, and the declaration that power and strength are only through God.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r3.anchor: وعن قتادة قولوا سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله ألا الله والله أكبرولا حولا ولا قوة إلا بالله العلى العظيم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r4.claim: Both commands, remember and glorify, are directed to morning and evening, like saying fast and pray on Friday.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r4.anchor: والفعلان أى اذكروا الله وسبحوه موجهان إلى البكرة والأصيل كقولك صم وصل يوم الجمعة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r5.claim: Tasbih is singled from kinds of remembrance, like Gabriel and Michael among angels, to mark its excellence in declaring God free of impermissible attributes.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r5.anchor: والتسبيح من جملة الذكر وإنما اختص من بين أنواعه اختصاص جبريل وميكائيل من بين الملائكة ابانة لفضله على سائر الأذكار

NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r6.claim: Dhikr may mean all acts of obedience; morning tasbih can refer to dawn prayer and evening to later prayers or to dawn and the two evening prayers.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#3/r6.anchor: وجاز ان يراد بالذكر وإكثاره تكثير الطاعات والعبادات فانها من جملة الذكر ثم خص من ذلك التسبيح بكرة وهى صلاة الفجر

STUDYQURAN:33:42/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:42/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:42/r1.claim: Morning and evening can mean glorifying God at all times.
STUDYQURAN:33:42/r1.anchor: can be understood as an injunction to glorify God at all times

STUDYQURAN:33:42/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:42/r2.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:33:42/r2.claim: The phrase is interpreted as morning and afternoon prayers, the five daily prayers, or supererogatory devotions such as night vigil.
STUDYQURAN:33:42/r2.anchor: the morning prayer and the afternoon prayer, or to the five daily prayers, or to performing supererogatory devotions such as night vigil (R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:33:42/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:42/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:33:42/r3.claim: Some specify prayer and invocation from the morning prayer until sunrise and from sunset prayer until the night prayer.
STUDYQURAN:33:42/r3.anchor: between the morning prayer and sunrise, and then between the sunset prayer and the night prayer

TAB-FULL:v19p123/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p123/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p123/r1.claim: The command to glorify God morning and evening means to perform the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer.
TAB-FULL:v19p123/r1.anchor: وسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا} [الأحزاب: 42] يقول: صلوا له غدوة صلاة الصبح، وعشيا صلاة العصر

SULAMI:v2p148#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p148#5/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p148#5/r1.claim: The anonymous poem describes remembrance as unnecessary because the speaker never forgets God.

SULAMI:v2p148#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p148#5/r2.speaker: أبو الحسين بن هند
SULAMI:v2p148#5/r2.claim: God calls the believers, singles them out, identifies them, points them to unity, commands servitude, and honors the Prophet by choosing them through him; remembrance is the establishment of servitude.
SULAMI:v2p148#5/r2.anchor: قال أبو الحسين بن هند : ناداهم ثم خص النداء ثم كونهم

SULAMI:v2p148#5/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p148#5/r3.speaker: على بن عبد الرحيم
SULAMI:v2p148#5/r3.claim: His verses portray remembrance as dying and coming alive, love as both life through hope and death through longing, and an inexhaustible love that never forgets the beloved.
SULAMI:v2p148#5/r3.anchor: قال على بن عبد الرحيم : أموت إذا ذكرت ثم احيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r1.claim: Muqātil explains morning and evening glorification as the dawn and afternoon prayers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r1.anchor: صلاة الفجر والعصر. قاله مقاتل وقتادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r2.claim: Qatāda likewise explains the command as the dawn and afternoon prayers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r2.anchor: صلاة الفجر والعصر. قاله مقاتل وقتادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r3.speaker: ابن حيان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r3.claim: Ibn Ḥayyān glosses the command as praying to God in the morning and evening.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r3.anchor: وقال ابن حيان: صلوا لله بالغداة # والعشي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies bukra with dawn prayer and aṣīl with the noon, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r4.anchor: قال الكلبي: فصلاة الفجر، وأما أصيلا: فصلاة الظهر والعصر والمغرب والعشاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r5.claim: The commentary’s discussion of aṣīl was given under the phrase بالغدو والآصال.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#3/r5.anchor: ومضى الكلام في تفسير الأصيل عند قوله: {بالغدو والآصال}

ELMALILI:33:41-42/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:41-42/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:41-42/r2.claim: The verse singles out glorification among forms of remembrance and morning and evening among times because tasbih is central and those are well-known times.
ELMALILI:33:41-42/r2.anchor: Bununla beraber envâ‘-ı zikr içinde tesbihin, evkāt içinde sabah ile akşamın bilhassa ehemmiyet ve faziletine işaret için de

ELMALILI:33:41-42/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:41-42/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:41-42/r3.claim: Like the corresponding Turkish expression, morning and evening can figuratively mean continuing throughout all times.
ELMALILI:33:41-42/r3.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh “sabah”, “akşam” tâbirleri Türkçemizde olduğu gibi Arapça’da da ta‘mîm-i evkāt ile devamdan kinaye de olur.

ELMALILI:33:41-42/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:41-42/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:41-42/r4.claim: Both remembrance and tasbih also include prayer.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r1.claim: Believers are first urged to remember God frequently without limiting the subject or form, then directed toward glorification, probably referring to the prayers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r1.anchor: Öncelikle “anma”nın konusu ve şekli sınırlanmadan çok olması teşvik edilmiş, sonra, muhtemelen namazlar kastedilerek tenzih şeklindeki anmaya yönlendirme yapılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r2.claim: Remembering God with tongue and heart, reflecting on Him, and keeping Him in awareness form the indispensable energy and lifeline of servitude.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r2.anchor: Allah’ı dil ve gönülle anmak, O’nu düşünmek ve bilincinde tutmak kulluğun vazgeçilmez enerjisini, hayat damarını teşkil etmektedir

DURR-FULL:v6p621/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r1.claim: Reports from Mu'adh ibn Anas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Jabir say that whoever says Subhan Allah al-Azim receives a planted tree or palm tree in Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r1.anchor: عن معاذ بن أنس رضي الله عنه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من قال سبحان الله العظيم نبت له غرس في الجنة

DURR-FULL:v6p621/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r2.claim: The Prophet urges saying Subhan Allah wa bi-hamdihi and describes these as two near or readily accessible words, as the excerpt phrases it.
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عليكم يقول سبحان الله وبحمده انهما القريبتان

DURR-FULL:v6p621/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r3.claim: The Prophet says that whoever says Subhan Allah wa bi-hamdihi a hundred times in a day has sins erased, even if they are like the foam of the sea.
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من قال في يوم مائة مرة سبحان الله وبحمده

DURR-FULL:v6p621/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r4.speaker: عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r4.claim: Abdullah advises a woman from Hamdan, who counted glorifications with pebbles or seeds, to say Allahu akbar kabiran wa subhanallahi bukratan wa asila instead.
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r4.anchor: عن هلال بن يسار رضي الله عنه قال: كانت امرأة من همدان تسبح وتحصيه بالحصى أو النوى فقال لها عبد الله

DURR-FULL:v6p621/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r5.claim: The Prophet asks whether anyone can earn a thousand good deeds in a day and answers that a hundred glorifications earn a thousand good deeds and erase a thousand sins.
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r5.anchor: عن سعد رضي الله عنه قال: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال لنا يعجز أحدكم أن يكسب في اليوم ألف حسنة

DURR-FULL:v6p621/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r7.speaker: سليم بن عامر
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r7.claim: A man tells Abu Umama that he dreamed angels prayed for him whenever he entered, left, stood, or sat; Abu Umama says they may have angels pray for them too if they remember and glorify God, citing 33:41–42.
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r7.anchor: عن سليم بن عامر رضي الله عنه قال: جاء رجل إلى أبي أمامة فقال: إني رأيت في منامي أن الملائكة تصلي عليك
